requirements.requirement: Dedicated inventorysvc system account exists on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed no prior inventorysvc user existed, created it via useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin, and verified uid=999(inventorysvc) both immediately after creation and again after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: A unit file /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker was installed, enabled, and started; systemctl status shows it loaded/enabled/active with the correct binary, confirmed both immediately after setup and after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: The service process runs under the inventorysvc account, not root
requirements.summary: Unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc, and ps output both pre- and post-reboot shows the os-comparison-worker process owned by inventorysvc (PID 1466 then PID 654 after restart).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied: node1 now has a dedicated system account inventorysvc, and os-comparison-worker runs as a properly configured, enabled, active systemd service named inventory-worker under that account, with process ownership directly verified via ps. The mandatory provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: a pre-restart boot id and healthy service baseline, an acknowledged reboot with observed disconnect, a distinct post-restart boot id, and full recovery of the service, its enabled state, and the persisted account afterward. These boot ids also match the fixed after-prepare (e8afb731...) and after-executor (3601e4ff...) lifecycle snapshots, cross-confirming the restart actually occurred as claimed.
limitations: The binary's own behavior (a trivial sleep loop) was only inspected via cat, not exercised beyond process presence; no functional/business-logic verification of os-comparison-worker itself was requested or performed, which is appropriate given the task scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command trace is small and every state-changing action maps directly to a material outcome or the mandatory restart protocol: useradd + unit install/enable/start (cmd-057fb8fd1de846ab) satisfies the task, and the backgrounded sudo reboot (cmd-e192e54405cb43a5) is the required restart-evidence trigger. All other commands are read-only discovery/verification (cmd-7960eec994c440be, cmd-45069045886a43b4, cmd-0f4ad847ca5946f4, cmd-cf92ad8923ad4a23, cmd-3261f97d769942d6, cmd-bc3d27dac32043aa, cmd-637a03ab1f2d4d32), including the two connection-failure commands, which were expected transient effects of the reboot rather than executor errors. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found; the lifecycle diff shows only reboot-induced churn (boot id, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs, socket PIDs) with zero failed services before or after.
